paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Job loses his health, and what he holds onto is his integrity. The LORD says it Himself: Job "still retains his integrity" (Job 2:3). Job's wife asks him, "Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die!" (Job 2:9), and Job turns it down. Faithfulness isn't something you only do when life is going well.

Now listen, because Job's answer is the one to remember. He asks, "Should we accept from God only good and not adversity?" (Job 2:10). The text says that "In all this, Job did not sin in what he said" (Job 2:10). I think that question is a tough one, and a good one to carry into your own hard days. Hard days don't have to push you away from God. You can bring the hurt to Him, and you can ask Him the hard questions too.

And look at what the friends do. They see how intense his suffering is, and they sit with him for seven days and seven nights, and no one says a word (Job 2:13). I think sometimes the best thing you can give a hurting person is just showing up. You don't always need the perfect words, friend. Job's story is far from over, so hold on to that.
